subject: Unacceptable decreasing fit in multigroup comparison

messages.author: b6689a9004e926b9
messages.subject: Unacceptable decreasing fit in multigroup comparison
parts:
Dear Lavaan Community, 
I was fitting a model, which is quite good in its fit indices and measurement blocks without any necessary modifications. The multigroup comparison (with SAM) worked as well. But I still have to test for  measurement invariance in order to proceeed with the coefficients comparison. (I am using the multigroup to test the categorical moderator).

 The time I was computing the multigroup CFA, my fit measures became worse (unacceptable) and I cannot find any reason for it. 

From the "normal" CFA without the grouping to the multigroup comparison:
 cfi :  0.943 --> 0.855
rmsea :0.055 --> 0.094
 srmr -->   0.047 -->0.080

My Syntax is pretty much the same for the grouping and non-grouping:

fit.mg_configurial <- cfa(messmodell103, data = myData3, estimator = "MLR",missing = "FIML",group = 'zufall',
              std.lv = TRUE)

fit.mg <- cfa(messmodell103, data = myData3, estimator = "MLR",missing = "FIML",
              std.lv = TRUE)

I did attach the output of my multigroup comparison with the bad fit indices.

I have to admit, that my sample is really really small given the high number of variables and a comparison between 4 groups (n= 301 with 25 missings). I still struggle if I can continue with the model due to that fact and was wondering if this might be the case for the bad fit. 

I was inspecting all groups, loadings and more and everything looks fine. All indicators are significantly loading on their respective variables with on exception in one group, but deleting the entire constructs is not changing the fit. 

I am very grateful about any idea what to further inspect as the source. 

Best regards, 
Madita

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Unacceptable decreasing fit in multigroup comparison
parts:
You have a huge model with 10 common factors, unlikely to be a perfect representation of the population.  When you go from 1 to multigroup, then you are trying to reproduce multiple (rather than 1 pooled) covariance matrix, so these misspecifications compound.  And the small samples in each group don't help (that inflates the chi-squared).  Even your full/pooled N is not large relative to the size of the model / number of estimated parameters.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

thank you very much for your response! This again confirms my suspicion that latent modeling is not possible with the small sample at least for this number of factors. Even with half the factors, the fit still becomes worse with the multigroup comparison.

Since I have already encountered the problem, I have run the model with factor scores and the Croon correction and used the SAM approach and command. The results remain stable compared to the latent modeling.
Do you know by chance if I can use a similar measurement invariance procedure as with the CFA with the SAM approach? Or should I compute the factor scores separately (which I didn't so far due to the Croon correction) and proceed with the multigroup CFA for the measurement invariance test?

Thank you so much in advance

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unacceptable decreasing fit in multigroup comparison
parts:
> Do you know by chance if I can use a similar measurement invariance
> procedure as with the CFA with the SAM approach?

The SAM approach was certainly not designed for this. The SAM approach
is all about the structural part of the model, and tries to 'isolate'
the measurement part from the structural part. In fact, the SAM approach
assumes that the measurement part of the model fits well, and is no
longer your primary concern.

Yves.
